merger_name: Nojima Corporation – Hitachi Global Life Solutions and Arçelik Hitachi Home Appliances

anzsic_codes.name: Other Electrical and Electronic Goods Wholesaling
Electrical, Electronic and Gas Appliance Retailing

merger_description:
Nojima Corporation (**Nojima**) is a Japanese consumer electronics and home appliances retailer. Nojima does not have any retail or wholesale operations in Australia.

Hitachi Global Life Solutions, Inc. (**Hitachi GLS**) manufactures and sells home and commercial appliances under the Hitachi brand, primarily in Japan. In 2021, Hitachi GLS and Arçelik A.Ş. (**Arçelik**), a Turkish domestic appliances and consumer electronics manufacturer, set up Arçelik Hitachi Home Appliances B.V. (**AHHA**), a joint venture to manufacture, sell and provide after-sales services of Hitachi-branded home appliances outside of Japan, including Australia. AHHA currently distributes Hitachi-branded refrigerators, washing machines, dryers and vacuum cleaners in Australia. Arçelik currently (that is, pre-Acquisition) holds a majority 60% stake in AHHA and Hitachi GLS holds the remaining 40%.

Nojima proposes to acquire the Hitachi-branded home appliances business through the acquisition of an 80.1% interest in GLS, Inc. (**GLS**), a new company that has been established by Hitachi GLS to consolidate its domestic (Japanese) home appliances business and AHHA (the **Acquisition**). As part of the Acquisition, Hitachi GLS will acquire Arçelik’s 60% stake in AHHA and will transfer its rights and obligations in respect of that acquisition to GLS.

Upon completion of the Acquisition, GLS will become a consolidated company of Nojima. Hitachi GLS will retain a 19.9% interest in GLS.

determination_table_content.details:
NJM4 Corporation, a special purpose vehicle managed by Nojima
Corporation (Nojima), proposes to acquire an 80.1% interest in
Hitachi Global Life Solutions’ (Hitachi GLS) home appliances
business and Arçelik Hitachi Home Appliances B.V. (AHHA)
(together, the Target) through a series of interconditional steps
(including Hitachi GLS’ acquisition of a 60% interest in AHHA), as
described in the transaction documents provided as part of the
application (the Acquisition).
Nojima, NJM4 Corporation and Hitachi GLS applied for a notification
waiver in respect of the Acquisition.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The acquirer, Nojima, is a Japanese consumer electronics and home
appliances retailer headquartered in Shinagawa, Tokyo and listed on
the Tokyo Stock Exchange. Nojima is primarily engaged in the retail
of consumer electronics and home appliances through an extensive
network of stores across Japan and in Southeast Asia (to a limited
extent). Nojima does not have any retail or wholesale operations in
Australia.
The Target comprises the Hitachi-branded home appliances
business, which manufactures and supplies Hitachi-branded home
appliances globally, including Hitachi GLS and AHHA. Hitachi GLS
manufactures and sells home and commercial appliances under the
Hitachi brand, primarily in Japan. Hitachi GLS and Arçelik A.Ş.
(Arçelik), a Turkish domestic appliances and consumer electronics
manufacturer, set up AHHA, a joint venture to manufacture, sell and
provide after-sales services of Hitachi-branded home appliances
outside of Japan, including Australia. Pre-Acquisition, Arçelik holds a
60% stake in AHHA and Hitachi GLS holds the remaining 40%.
AHHA currently distributes Hitachi-branded refrigerators, washing
machines, dryers and vacuum cleaners in Australia. Hitachi GLS
does not have any presence in Australia separate from AHHA.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition. In particular:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between Nojima and Hitachi
GLS (including its connected entities) or between Nojima
and AHHA in the manufacture and supply of refrigerators,
washing machines, dryers or vacuum cleaners in Australia
b. there are alternative manufacturers and suppliers of
refrigerators, washing machines, dryers and vacuums in
Australia
c. there is a low risk of foreclosure or other concerning vertical
effects resulting from exclusionary conduct in Australia
post-acquisition.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
